answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or vote on reputation updates. A Sybil attacker can create thousands of keys, but each one must fund its own bond; copying software does not multiply the stake. If an identity is caught colluding or delivering fabricated work, peers can prove the violation and slash its bond, making mass identities costly to maintain and risky to deploy. The walnut orchard’s tide-based delivery schedule may be public, but the bond requirement still makes each fake account pay its way.
